chapters.heading: UNITED STATES CAPITOL POLICE REFORM AND ACCOUNTABILITY

sections.heading: Executive noninterference and interagency assistance
paragraphs: (a) The Capitol Police shall be a legislative-branch law-enforcement agency. Except as expressly provided by law, the Capitol Police shall not be subject to the direction, command, supervision, suspension, discipline, control, or operational authority of the President, the Department of Justice, the Department of Homeland Security, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the United States Secret Service, the Armed Forces, or any other executive department, agency, officer, or employee with respect to congressional security, access to the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds, chamber security, legislative proceedings, protection of Members of Congress, protection of officers of Congress, enforcement of House or Senate rules, or the internal security operations of Congress.

(b) No executive department, agency, officer, or employee may direct, command, countermand, delay, suspend, interfere with, or otherwise control an action of the Capitol Police concerning congressional security, access to the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds, chamber security, legislative proceedings, protection of Members of Congress, protection of officers of Congress, enforcement of House or Senate rules, or the internal operations of Congress, except where such executive department, agency, officer, or employee is acting under an express Act of Congress, a lawful court order, a lawful request for assistance, an emergency authority otherwise provided by law, or another lawful authority that does not place the Capitol Police under executive command.

(c) The Capitol Police may request, receive, and coordinate assistance from any federal, State, local, tribal, territorial, military, or other lawful authority when such assistance is necessary to protect Congress, respond to an emergency, investigate a threat, provide protective services, secure a congressional proceeding, support a temporary jurisdiction operation, or carry out the lawful duties of the Capitol Police.

(d) The Chief may request emergency assistance from an outside agency without prior approval of the Capitol Police Board where delay would endanger life, expose Congress or a protected person to an imminent threat, impair an active emergency response, or prevent the Capitol Police from preserving order or securing official congressional business.

(e) The Chief shall obtain approval of the Board before entering into any continuing agreement, memorandum of understanding, joint operating procedure, data-sharing arrangement, task force assignment, reimbursement agreement, support agreement, or operational arrangement with an executive department, executive agency, State, local government, military authority, foreign entity, private entity, or other outside organization.

(f) Any outside assistance received by the Capitol Police shall remain subject to this Act, the authority of the Board, the command of the Chief, and the authority of each House over its own chamber, proceedings, rules, privileges, and controlled spaces.

(g) An outside agency assisting the Capitol Police shall not acquire command over Capitol Police officers, control over congressional spaces, authority over chamber proceedings, or power to enforce House or Senate rules unless such authority is expressly provided by law or by lawful order of the relevant House.

(h) The Capitol Police may provide assistance to another law enforcement agency where the assistance is connected to the protection of Congress, a Member of Congress, an officer of Congress, a congressional employee, a witness, an invited guest, a congressional proceeding, or a threat involving official congressional business.

(i) The Capitol Police shall not be assigned to an executive branch investigation, operation, task force, intelligence activity, security detail, or enforcement action unless the assignment is connected to congressional security, authorized by the Board, or necessary during an emergency involving Congress or a protected person.

(j) No officer of the Capitol Police may be ordered by an executive official to enforce a political directive, interfere with a congressional proceeding, deny lawful access to a Member of Congress, execute an order against either House, or take any action inconsistent with the lawful duties of the Capitol Police.

(k) The Department of Justice may prosecute offenses against the United States arising from conduct investigated by the Capitol Police, and the Capitol Police may refer criminal matters to the Department of Justice or another lawful prosecuting authority.

(l) A referral to the Department of Justice or another prosecuting authority shall not transfer command of the Capitol Police, waive the privileges of either House, or authorize executive control over congressional security operations. (m)The Chief shall maintain records of interagency assistance requested, received, or provided under this section, including the agency involved, the purpose of assistance, the authority relied upon, the duration of assistance, the personnel assigned, and whether any arrest, detention, use of force, injury, search, seizure, intelligence activity, or major security incident occurred.

(n) The Chief shall report to the Board as soon as practicable any interagency assistance involving an emergency, a major security event, an executive department, a military authority, a deployment outside the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds, an arrest, a detention, a use of force, a threat to a Member of Congress, or a matter substantially affecting the operations or independence of the Capitol Police.

(o) Nothing in this section shall be construed to prevent the Department of Justice, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the United States Secret Service, the Department of Homeland Security, the Armed Forces, a court of competent jurisdiction, or any other lawful authority from exercising independent authority otherwise provided by the Constitution or laws of the United States, including authority to enforce federal criminal law, investigate offenses within lawful jurisdiction, execute warrants, execute court orders, prosecute offenses, protect persons lawfully under their protection, respond to emergencies, share threat information, provide technical assistance, provide emergency assistance, or coordinate with the Capitol Police.

(p) Nothing in this section shall be construed to prevent the Capitol Police from requesting, receiving, or coordinating assistance from an executive department, executive agency, military authority, State, local government, or other lawful authority as provided by this Act.

(q) The receipt of assistance, referral of a criminal matter, sharing of threat information, participation in emergency coordination, execution of a court order, or cooperation with a lawful investigation shall not be construed to transfer command of the Capitol Police, waive the privileges of either House, subject the Capitol Police to executive supervision, or authorize executive control over congressional security operations.

(r) Where an executive department, agency, officer, or employee acts under independent legal authority within or near the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds, such action shall, to the greatest extent practicable and consistent with law and emergency necessity, be coordinated with the Chief, the Capitol Police Board, or the relevant Sergeant at Arms where the action may affect congressional proceedings, chamber access, congressional security, protected persons, or areas under the control of either House.
